observation_summary: The solver throws an IllegalArgumentException when one of the provided endpoints is a root of the function.
reasoning_summary: The BrentSolver implementation strictly enforces that the function values at the provided endpoints must have different signs (yMin * yMax < 0). However, it fails to account for cases where one of the endpoints is exactly a root (i.e., yMin == 0 or yMax == 0). In such cases, the product yMin * yMax is 0, which triggers an IllegalArgumentException even though the root is already identified at the boundary. The code lacks a check to return the endpoint as the root when the function value at that endpoint is zero.
